sources.title: A Goodbye to Gravity
sources.locator: Written body: observation/cause distinction; aether discussion; four elements near conclusion
sources.summary: Young separates falling from its proposed cause and offers an aether-medium account, including elemental motion. His physical and geocentric claims remain his positions; this review does not verify them.

sources.title: Elemental Constitution of Soul & Substance
sources.locator: Introduction: four-element proportions; planetary metals; humour system
sources.summary: The introduction connects elemental proportions with substances and soul. The quotation attributed to Paracelsus has not been checked against Paracelsus.

sources.title: Alchemy of the Microcosm — Flesh, Food & The Rivers of the Liver
sources.summary: Young names Salt, Sulphur and Mercury and frames body/realm correspondence through microcosm and macrocosm. The introduction does not supply complete definitions or warrant medical conclusions.

sources.title: The Aether Conspiracy - How Science Conceals Spirit
sources.locator: Page introduction: fifth element and connecting medium
sources.summary: The introduction presents aether as a connecting fifth element. Its historical and physical claims require separate examination.

sources.locator: Printed p138 / extraction PAGE148: Chemistry of Creation; printed p141 / extraction PAGE151: Mercury the Messenger
sources.summary: Selected passages distinguish the Three Primes from literal substances and enumerate four Mercury senses. OCR wording needs facsimile verification before direct quotation.

sources.locator: Sections 4 Vocabulary Recoding, 6 What Young Challenges, 10 Metadata
sources.summary: Historical generated dossier prescribes technical recoding of religious terms and asserts framework validation. Its creation label does not date author belief or establish author adoption.

sources.locator: Governing authorial direction; How this changes the writer
sources.summary: Existing author direction keeps scale and encounter independent and revises meaning through action and consequence.
Older writing contains both useful voice and recurring scaffolding; age alone cannot confer preferred style or factual validity.
